site.title: Preserve Honeoye Falls
site.description: Preserve Honeoye Falls or PHF is a grassroots organization founded by residents from the village of Honeoye Falls and the neighboring town of Mendon in response to a large-scale housing development called Copperfield that is being proposed for Honeoye Falls.

hero.eyebrow: "Come for the charm, stay for the experience" -- Honeoye Falls village motto
hero.headline: Keep Honeoye Falls
hero.intro:
A developer wants to build a large, tract housing development called Copperfield on village farmland. This project is bad for the village and the community that calls Honeoye Falls and Mendon home. 

**The project CANNOT proceed without village approval and NO approval has been given as of now. There is still time to make your voice heard!**

copperfield.body:
The scale and scope of the Copperfield housing development is unprecedented in the history of Honeoye Falls. Among other things, the plan calls for the construction of a 170-unit apartment building up to 52 feet tall (by far the tallest, privately-owned structure in all of Mendon of which Honeoye Falls is a part) and 200-plus homes, all squeezed into 179 acres of what is now village farmland.

The current development plan does not comply with current village zoning laws, including the village's own updated Comprehensive Plan that was adopted in 2022 after lengthy study and public consultation with village stakeholders and residents. [insert link to CP somewhere https://www.villageofhoneoyefalls.gov/DocumentCenter/View/349/2021-Comprehensive-Plan]

copperfield.title: What is Copperfield?
copperfield.sources: Sources: the applicant's Preliminary Engineer's Report (June 2026), traffic study (Dec. 2025), Environmental Assessment Form and plan sheets; 2020 U.S. Census.
copperfield.lede: Morrell Builders, a developer in Victor, has proposed a large subdivision of single and multi-family homes to be built on 179 acres of farmland. This land is located inside four main village thoroughfares: Main St (Route 65), East Street, Cheese Factory Road and Quaker Meeting House Road.

concerns.title: Many Questions But No Answers
concerns.lede: According to a 2013 village survey, the number one reason residents cited for why they chose to live in Honeoye Falls was because of the village's "small town/village atmosphere." The proposed Copperfield development would fundamentally change the character of Honeoye Falls, gutting the village of its "small town" culture and putting it on the path to becoming another failed experiment in "suburban sprawl".

items.title: Traffic the Village Cannot Handle
items.text: The village's own Comprehensive Plan singled out "traffic" as a key "weakness" affecting the viability of Honoeye Falls. That was in 2020. Since that time, traffic in the village has only increased, with the development of more housing units. Copperfield will bring even more traffic to Honeoye Falls that will stretch its limited road network to a breaking point. Neither the village nor Morrell Builders, the developer of Copperfield, has proposed any road improvements to accommodate the unprecedented increase in car and truck traffic that Copperfield will create in and around Honeoye Falls.

items.title: Expenses the Village Cannot Afford
items.text: Studies have shown that the additional tax revenue new residents provide a municipality are almost always offset, and sometimes even overtaken, by the money that needs to be spent on public services for those residents. One would think that given the size and scale of a project like Copperfield, a fiscal impact study would be conducted to assess the way in which such a large scale development would impact the financial health of the village. Yet no such study has been done. Why?

items.title: Environmental Impact the Village Cannot Absorb
items.text: The wastewater treatment and storm sewer facilities that serve Honeoye Falls residents are notoriously old and already strained in their capacity to handle the needs of the current village population. Clay pipes. Poorly drained properties. Inadequate storm sewer drainage. These are just some of the problems that plague the village's aging infrastructure, according to studies conducted for the 2022 Comprehensive Plan. Without further study, planning and investment, a massive tract housing project that paves over existing village farmland and adds hundreds of new homes and at least a thousand more residents will create shockwaves to the village's aging infrastructure that it will not be able to handle.

items.title: A full environmental review
items.text: A project this size calls for a full Environmental Impact Statement that looks at all phases together, along with Wolfsberger Park and other planned development, before any decision is made.

items.title: What comes next
items.text: We worry that a development this size at the edge of the Village, with 1,000+ new residents and hundreds more cars at rush hour, will invite drive-throughs, franchises and other unwanted development.

about.title: Who we are
about.body:
Preserve Honeoye Falls is a nonpartisan group of Village of Honeoye Falls and Town of Mendon residents. We came together in 2026 when the Copperfield proposal reached the Zoning Board of Appeals.

We have filed to incorporate as a New York not-for-profit so we can raise and manage money responsibly and work with experienced land-use counsel. Everything we share comes from public documents: the developer's own application, letters from state and local agencies, official meeting minutes, and the Village's Comprehensive Plan.
